text:
Avery Johnson: Need quick swarm on a high-stakes ref call request. Prospect is *BluePeak Financial* (late-stage, security-heavy). They asked for a customer who’s running Dedicated with strict latency SLOs + can speak to fallback/rollouts. Thinking QuantaPay.

Avery Johnson: Two asks:
1) which SE should attend (ideally someone who’s been close to QuantaPay’s POC + can talk through the Console dashboards without oversharing)
2) what do we need to prep QuantaPay *not* to cover (pricing, security details, etc.)

Grace O'Connor: Adding context: BluePeak wants the call next week, 30 mins. They’re specifically worried about “latency variance during bursts” + “what happens when a model rollout goes sideways.”

Priyom Das: +1 QuantaPay is the right match. I can ask their champion (Anika) today if they’re willing to do a call Tue/Wed.

Hannah Schmitt: Are we sure QuantaPay is cleared for reference calls already? Last I saw, public case study was conditional but ref calls were “ok with guardrails”.

Rachel Kim: Ref-call-only is green *if* we keep it to the approved boundaries. No public materials, no logos, no screenshots shared externally. We need to send QuantaPay the prep sheet + topics to avoid.

Miguel Santos: I can run prep with Anika 15 mins before the call. She’s generally good but tends to “get into the weeds” on infra.

Markus Klein: SE attendee: recommend either @Simran Kaur (knows the Dedicated benchmarking + rollout/fallback mechanics) or @Liam O'Rourke (good at guiding refs live + keeping us on message). I’d lean Liam for *call control*, Simran for *deep technical*.

Simran Kaur: I can join if we expect detailed questions on batching/latency tuning, but I agree Liam is better as the “air cover” to keep it clean.

Liam O'Rourke: Happy to attend. If we do it, I want a tight pre-brief:
- what BluePeak can ask
- what QuantaPay can share
- 2–3 “anchor stories” we want them to tell (rollout safety, predictable p95, incident handling)

Avery Johnson: Love it. Let’s do Liam as primary SE, Simran optional/backup if it turns super technical.

Priyom Das: Works. BluePeak’s technical buyer is their platform lead. They’ll ask about:
- “dedicated pool sizing / burst behavior”
- “fallback policy to smaller variant if capacity constrained”
- “how quickly do you detect regressions”

Rachel Kim: Topics to avoid (for QuantaPay prep):
- Exact $ pricing / discounts / commit terms (just say “commercials vary; talk to your AE”)
- Any customer-specific security controls details (KMS config, audit log schemas, IP ranges, vendor lists)
- Exact GPU types/counts, regions, or capacity allocations
- Mentioning any competitors by name or doing vendor comparisons
- Sharing screenshots of Console dashboards (they can describe what they *monitor*)

Miguel Santos: Also: no internal incident IDs / ticket numbers. If they bring up regressions, keep it at “we saw a latency regression during benchmarking and worked with Redwood to resolve within X days” level.

Hannah Schmitt: +1. Prospect loves to ask “what’s the worst outage you’ve had” — we should give QuantaPay a safe answer template.

Liam O'Rourke: Suggest we give QuantaPay a “safe phrasing” block:
- “We had a performance regression during a controlled test window; Redwood provided visibility + mitigation; we validated p95 back within our target before expanding traffic.”
No dates, no version numbers.

Markus Klein: On what to highlight (for BluePeak’s concerns):
- Dedicated = predictable baseline throughput
- Console = token/latency breakdown; ability to see p50/p95 and error rates
- Rollouts = canary + automatic fallback policy
- Operational support loop (SE/Support responsiveness) without quoting any SLA language

Avery Johnson: Perfect. Rachel/Miguel—can you drop the latest internal “Reference Call Prep One Pager” link here? I’ll send to BluePeak internally + to Priyom for QuantaPay prep.

Rachel Kim: Here’s the internal template (do not forward externally): https://drive.google.com/…/Reference_Call_Prep_One_Pager_(Internal)
I’ll clone a version for QuantaPay with the “avoid topics” section pre-filled.

Priyom Das: I’ll email Anika with proposed times + confirm she’s comfortable with the boundaries (ref call only, no screenshots, no pricing).

Grace O'Connor: Logistics: BluePeak asked for 2 attendees max on Redwood side. So: Avery + Liam. If Simran is backup, she can be on standby but not on the calendar unless needed.

Simran Kaur: Fine by me. If needed, Liam can ping me live and I’ll jump in.

Liam O'Rourke: For call structure (30 mins):
- 5 mins intros + context
- 15 mins QuantaPay story (what they built, why Dedicated, what they measure)
- 8 mins Q&A
- 2 mins wrap (next steps through AE)
Avery, I’ll send you 5 discovery prompts you can use to steer if it drifts.

Avery Johnson: Great. Priyom—once Anika confirms, loop in Miguel for the pre-brief. Goal is to have QuantaPay fully prepped *before* we confirm with BluePeak.

Miguel Santos: On it. I’ll do a quick “do/don’t” rundown + align on the 2–3 anchor points.

Hannah Schmitt: One more: remind QuantaPay they can always say “I’m not sure / I’ll defer to Redwood” rather than guessing. Better to pause than improvise.

Rachel Kim: Yes. I’ll include that in the prep doc as an explicit line.

Avery Johnson: Thanks all. This one matters — BluePeak is forecast-critical. :thumbsup:
